data.relationship: AI data-center colocation capacity leased to AMD - 530 MW across five campuses on 15-year leases (direct triple-net at Pecos, Hunt and Muskogee, plus AMD-credit-supported neocloud leases at Auburn and Dalton)
data.signal: Commercial partnership with AMD for up to 2.5 GW of data center capacity. The initial agreement represents more than $14 billion of base contracted revenue across 15-year agreements with 2.5% annual escalators, with Core Scientific delivering 530 MW across five sites: approximately 380 MW directly to AMD under a triple-net lease across Pecos, Hunt and Muskogee, and the remaining approximately 150 MW across Auburn and Dalton supporting an unnamed neocloud under a modified gross lease for which AMD provides full credit support for the full 15-year term. The credit support carries no equity step-in rights, protecting Core Scientific's equity in the projects. Core Scientific issued AMD a warrant struck at current market levels, vesting subject to certain commercial conditions. The platform is an integrated colocation platform engineered to support AMD Helios rack-scale systems, with a close-coupled design framework aligned to AMD's GPU and CPU technology roadmap. Pecos is the lead site with initial megawatt delivery in the first half of 2027; about half the contract delivers in 2027 and half in 2028. The build requires approximately $6 billion of capital at $11 million-$12 million per megawatt, to be financed through project-level bonds. AMD additionally holds an exclusive reservation right on as much as two additional gigawatts at Pecos, Hunt and Muskogee.
data.units: 530 MW across five campuses (~380 MW direct triple-net + ~150 MW AMD-credit-supported neocloud lease); up to 2.5 GW including the reservation

data.signal: CEO Hock Tan disclosed the multi-die XPU roadmap in explicit terms - the clearest statement yet of how Broadcom is 'substituting Moore's law with something else'. He said Moore's law has ended ('Moving down process node, you cannot achieve double transistor performance anymore. You barely eke out 5% improvement, but you get power'), that physics caps a single die at '800 square millimeters' ('That's the largest size die you can make'), and that Broadcom now puts '2 die together in one chip. So effectively, you now have 1,600 square millimeters, double.' Critically: 'The current generation we are working on has 4 dies. You can just imagine. The one after that probably will go to maybe no limit, 8 die. 8 die in one chip. So your chip size is equivalent of, say, 800 times 8, over 6,000 square millimeter running as one single chip.' He stressed this enabling technology 'is not just created at a wafer fab or with the memory guys. It is us designing it', and listed the moats as high-speed SerDes/IO IP, multiplier density per square millimeter, die-to-die communication at low power, and advanced packaging.
data.figure: largest size die you can make 800 square millimeters; 2 die = 1,600 square millimeters; current generation has 4 dies; next probably 8 die in one chip = over 6,000 square millimeter; process node shrink now yields barely 5% improvement

data.signal: Roadmap beyond the first OpenAI XPU (the Jalapeño itself was already disclosed on the Q3 FY2026 call): Tan said the relationship 'is very strong and continues to be very strong because we are working on the next and two generations to the Jalapeño' - i.e. two further generations already in development. He also explained why the first one took only a year ('within a year, we created an XPU called the Jalapeño'): co-design, where the customer's frontier-model team translates model specs into the architecture of what the compute hardware needs and Broadcom supplies the micro-architecture and physical design - 'When you have that very tight, almost seamless flow, it's not that much a challenge to be able to create chips of that caliber that quickly.'
data.figure: no specific figure

data.signal: Tan unpacked what 'supply constrained' means behind the 2027 and 2028 AI revenue forecast, and it is not silicon. On chips: 'We understand the need for wafers, leading-edge wafers, and memory, as well as even substrates. That is pretty well locked in. We can pretty well lock that in for sure in 2027, and the process of locking in 2028 gives us within some limits. That is more within our control.' The less deterministic constraint is a site that is power READY, not merely power available: 'If you want to make it power ready, say, in 2028, got to start construction on the sites now. That is not us, our customers, has to start construction on the site now to make it available and ready by 2028' - a year and a half to two years out, gated by transformers, gas turbines, local permitting and the rate of construction. 'It's a judged number based on not just supply of memory wafers, but availability and readiness of power sites.'
data.figure: wafers, memory and substrates locked in for 2027, being locked for 2028

data.signal: Customer concentration and the financing vehicle, in Tan's own words: 'we have only six customers today at this point. Very concentrated group, but I believe these six customers, all each of them are creating their own frontier models'. Of those six, 'two of them, two of the strongest guys do not have the cash flows to be able to generate the compute needed to train and create inference, productize their models' - he later referred to financing partners 'Anthropic and OpenAI'. Why Broadcom backs all six rather than picking: 'we cannot tell who is going to win' and 'they may coexist'. On the already-disclosed XPV platform he drew the line Broadcom had not drawn before: 'We do it by creating a platform, we call it XPV, where it would enable them to be financed. We do not finance directly.' Tan also rejected the circularity charge head-on: 'This is not circular financing... We are using financing to create demand. Demand is there' - when a customer sees the demand and could buy the compute from someone else, it is not circular.
data.figure: only six customers today; two of the strongest do not have the cash flows

data.signal: Tan gave the unit economics he uses to judge AI durability - useful as the demand test behind Broadcom's XPU forecast. On a single deployment: 'Take the case of a very good frontier model. 1 gigawatt could generate $30 billion ARR... The cost to run 1 gigawatt, as you all know, is about $10 billion a year. So you have $20 billion that accrue to the model guys and the application that goes with it, and $10 billion fought over by the power guys, the cloud provider guys, even the chip and memory guys.' On the industry today (inference only, sourced from OpenRouter and Vercel data): global token generation cost is 'around $200 billion a year now' against model-layer revenue of 'Around $150 billion'. Splitting it: more than half of tokens are generated on open weight models, but frontier closed models take 'at least' 75% of the revenue - 'That's $120 billion. They spend roughly $100 billion' - while open weight players spend 'the other $100 billion' for 'revenue $30 billion'. His conclusion: value accrues to the best frontier models, which is why Broadcom's XPU customers must be frontier-model developers.
data.figure: 1 gigawatt generates $30 billion ARR at about $10 billion a year to run, leaving $20 billion to the model layer and $10 billion to power, cloud, chip and memory; industry token cost around $200 billion a year vs around $150 billion model revenue; frontier models 75% of revenue = $120 billion on roughly $100 billion spend; open weight revenue $30 billion on the other $100 billion

data.signal: CY2026 outlook: Applied expects to grow its semiconductor equipment business more than 20% this calendar year, with demand weighted to the second half and availability of customer cleanroom space the key factor pacing investment; largest customers are giving longer-term visibility and strong growth momentum is expected to carry into 2027 (CEO: '27 is shaping up to be another strong year). Applied has nearly doubled its system manufacturing capacity over the past several years and still has prepositioned space to scale much higher; it increased inventory by nearly $500 million year-over-year for rising build plans (inventory days approximately 153, not expected to rise much) and is giving its approximately 2,000 suppliers longer visibility and specific bills of material. data.signal: Leading-edge logic: customers are adding capacity at FinFET nodes while ramping gate-all-around nodes, which grow Applied's available market considerably and give multiple points of share gain. CEO said Applied is #1 and on track to capture more than 50% of its served market in gate-all-around and wiring, including backside power, and is #1 in deposition, conductor etch and packaging. Applied plans to launch more than a dozen new products in 2026, including 3 for advanced logic and DRAM announced the week of the call: the Viva radical treatment system (angstrom-level engineering of nanosheet surfaces for faster gate-all-around transistors), Sym3 Z Magnum (newest Sym3 etch variant for critical etch steps in gate-all-around transistors and advanced DRAM) and the Spectral ALD system (selective deposition of monocrystalline moly, reducing contact resistance in advanced logic devices by up to 15%). Applied is leading the transition from ALD tungsten to ALD moly in logic contact formation, while copper PVD steps keep growing and remain an order of magnitude larger than ALD moly.

data.signal: DELL RUNS 'FOUR MOVING TO FIVE' DIFFERENT SOURCES OF TOKENS - THE TOKEN-ECONOMICS CASE FOR HYBRID/ON-PREM INFRASTRUCTURE. Global CTO and Chief AI Officer John Roese said the first principle of token economics in the agentic era 'is you have got to have a diverse source of intelligence... sources that range from different compliance levels, different capabilities, but also different economic strata. At Dell Technologies, I have four moving to five different fundamental sources of tokens. They have very different economics. I run open models on-prem in my data centers. I run frontier models in my data centers. I run frontier models in VPCs I control. I use APIs. I now run models on devices using things like personal agent frameworks.' He grounded it in unit economics: an agent that helps the CEO decide in real time can be worth '$100,000 a month to run', while an agent cleaning CRM records where 'each CRM record it cleans up has an economic value of $0.50' needs an environment where 'it does not cost $12 in tokens to do a $0.50 task'. A customer on 'a single provider with a single set of models over a single economic model... fundamentally wouldn't be able to do the CRM agent because it's just not affordable in that model' - the demand argument for on-prem and VPC inference capacity rather than API-only consumption.
data.figure: four moving to five fundamental sources of tokens (on-prem open, on-prem frontier, VPC frontier, API, on-device); $100,000 a month agent vs a $0.50 CRM record that must not cost $12 in tokens

data.signal: Capital and capex: IREN secured underwriting commitments for $3.6 billion of GPU financing, a delayed-draw term loan from Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan that amortizes in full over its 5-year term. The loan is secured against the GPUs and Microsoft's contracted cash flows, with interest expected to be less than 6%. Together with Microsoft's $1.9 billion in prepayments, it covers 95% of the GPU-related CapEx for Horizons 1 through 4; Roberts put the average interest rate at around 3% once prepayments are factored in. Financial year-to-date, IREN has secured $9.2 billion from customer prepayments, convertible notes (including the $2.3 billion issued in December), GPU leasing arrangements and the dedicated Microsoft GPU financing. The CFO's capex breakdown: $5.8 billion of compute CapEx for Microsoft plus approximately $3 billion of data center CapEx (a material amount already incurred or committed); with the GPU financing and balance-sheet cash, 'all of the Microsoft related CapEx for the compute and DC' is spoken for. The remaining ARR-target expansion at Prince George and Mackenzie needs circa $3 billion of CapEx; a material amount of that has already been incurred and financed through lease-based financing. Next financing priorities are data center financing for Horizons 1 through 4 once they come online, plus select corporate-level facilities.

data.signal: Secured power: IREN secured a new 1.6 gigawatt data center campus in Oklahoma, a very large site in the Southwest Power Pool immediately adjacent to a major utility substation, with low-latency connectivity to major network exchanges and a ramp schedule starting in 2028. The site takes total secured power to over 4.5 gigawatts and extends IREN's US pipeline beyond ERCOT. IREN also cited 810 megawatts of operating air-cooled data centers and 3.6 gigawatts of greenfield data center sites. On ERCOT's new batch study process, management believes Sweetwater 1 and 2 would be included in batch 0, which would mean the full 2 gigawatts is secured; the interconnection agreement was signed in 2023. Sweetwater 1 remains on track to energize in Q2, with full bulk substations capable of 1.4 gigawatts, and procurement and civil works are underway for the first phase of Sweetwater data centers. Roberts: 'time to power is critical, but time to data centers is actually the more limiting factor.'

data.signal: Build progress: at Prince George (British Columbia), data center fit-outs for air-cooled NVIDIA B200 and B300 GPUs are complete and are waiting for the remaining GPUs on order. At Mackenzie and Canal Flats, teams are preparing the sites for AI cloud expansion with the same playbook used at Prince George ('ASICs are coming out of those data centers and GPUs are going in'). At Childress, construction across Horizons 1 to 4 is on schedule to meet Microsoft's GPU deployment timelines. Management said the long-lead procurement and skilled-labor constraints seen across the industry are manageable for IREN because it builds continuously and has a team of over 2,000 people. It named the pace of construction, not power or capital, as the current constraint on the phased Sweetwater build-out.

data.signal: Demand and pricing: 'demand is not the constraint for us.' IREN is in multiple advanced negotiations for larger-scale deployments with hyperscale and non-hyperscale counterparties. Hyperscalers and AI enterprises are increasingly focused on air-cooled GPUs because they deploy faster, which suits IREN's 810 megawatts of operating air-cooled data centers. Customers are more open to longer tenures than before, seeing 'a long-dated supply-demand imbalance', and continue to make prepayments. IREN keeps signing contracts for both new and prior-generation GPUs. According to management, newer chips go mostly to training while older ones shift toward inference. Chief Commercial Officer Kent Draper said there is 'an undersupply relative to demand' and that A100s, more than 5 years old, are 'still effectively 100% utilized across the industry'. He added that IREN expects chips to stay economically useful beyond its contract lengths, including the 5-year Microsoft contract.

data.signal: Strategy: IREN prefers AI cloud to colocation because power, and above all data center capacity, is scarce. Roberts said every incremental 200 megawatts can deliver either '$300 million-ish through a co-location or multiples of that in the billions under a cloud contract', though IREN would still pursue a compelling colocation deal. Most demand is bare-metal from hyperscalers and large AI firms, and software is a small share; even so, one contract under negotiation is 'a multibillion-dollar contract where we need to bring a software solution'. Asked about NVIDIA credit backstops for neoclouds, Roberts said it is 'a safe assumption' that IREN is having 'very similar, if not exact same dialogue' with all these counterparties about structures such as equity investments, credit backstops and offtake agreements.

Digital Realty leans on its five-gigawatt power bank. 'Data center supply remains tight, especially within our footprint'; availability across the 800 megawatts in-place Northern Virginia portfolio 'remains very limited, with strong demand queuing for the 300 megawatts of capacity we are readying for delivery in the 2027 to 2029 time frame.' The CEO said 2027 deliveries are 'pretty exceptional and sought after' with multiple customers per capacity block, 2028 should be as attractive, and the company is 'not seeing a tremendous amount of competitive unleashed capacity'; labor is 'getting challenging more challenging by the day', though every project in the 10 plus billion under construction has workforce and supply chain security. The CIO expects demand to increase two and a half to three times over the next five years against severely constrained supply (power, nimbyism, zoning). On an IT load basis, occupancy was approximately 91% (same capital) and 89% (total portfolio) at year-end, with reporting moving to power-based metrics.

data.signal: INTEL'S EXPLANATION OF THE CPU SHORTAGE - AGENTIC WORKLOADS RUN ON CPUs BETWEEN TOKEN GENERATIONS: Nanduri said that in agentic systems the tokens produce outcomes that must be executed and verified, and 'CPUs start to play a lot of role because CPUs are their execution engine, verification engine, and your sandboxing engine. If you see recently why are CPUs in a shortage is because a lot of these back and forth ping pong is happening in the system.' He framed the data-center buildout as four planes - a control plane (orchestrator / agent router / model router / security harness) that runs on CPUs, an agent or data plane for token generation across CPUs, GPUs and RDUs, a network plane where scale-up and scale-out determine wall-clock time as models cross chip boundaries, and a storage plane for databases, KV cache and context memory pooling, all hosted with a CPU - and said memory cost increases have made this balance, rather than raw token throughput, the ROI question for enterprises.

data.signal: AGENTIC WORKLOADS ARE THE CPU DEMAND DRIVER, AND IRELAND IS THE SUPPLY ANSWER: CFO David Zinsner quantified the workload shift for the first time - comparing a regular training data center with an agentic-like activity, 'it's like a 4 to 6 increase in CPU requirements'. Server CPU units, which used to decline low single digits, are now growing double digits with core counts growing at multiples of that, and ASP per core - which fell almost 20% in some years - has at least stabilized and in some like-for-like cases is going up, so core-count growth now flows straight through to revenue. The constraint is supply, not competitive performance: 'as we look at this year, next year, probably even into 2028, this is going to be less about competitive performance of CPUs and more about can you get the CPUs to the customer', and share will follow whoever can supply. Granite Rapids, the data-center flagship, is built in Ireland on Intel 3; part of next year's CapEx is to ramp Ireland where Intel wants to 'more than double the output there next year'. Even so Intel will 'under-supply for sure this year', 'probably under-supply next year', and hopes to be in a good position by 2028.
data.figure: 4 to 6 increase in CPU requirements; more than double the output there next year

data.signal: MEMORY PRICING IS KILLING CLIENT DEMAND, AND INTEL DELIBERATELY REDIRECTED THAT CAPACITY TO DATA CENTER: Zinsner said Intel made a conscious decision at the beginning of the year, seeing that memory pricing would 'start to destroy some of the demand on the client side' - it focused client CPU capacity on big-core products, yielded small-core parts to others, and shifted as much supply as possible to data center on the strength of long-term agreements with data-center customers. Intel 3 cannot flex (Meteor Lake was the only client product in Ireland and is rolling off as Panther Lake ramps), so more Granite Rapids output has to come from new capacity, throughput and yields; but moving client off Intel 7 onto Intel 18A frees Intel 7 capacity that is being used to supply the data-center market. He called the client weakness 'probably the best thing we could have, given the data center demand', and expects the memory hangover to persist into next year before snapping back through 2027.

data.signal: HIGH BANDWIDTH COMPUTE (HBC) IS AN EXPLICIT ALTERNATIVE TO HBM, WITH SPECS AND A SHIP DATE. Durga Malladi (EVP Tech Planning, Edge & Data Center): HBC puts compute right next to memory and was 'a direct take on an alternative way of doing things as opposed to HBM'. Claimed '6x improvement compared to HBM in terms of tokens per second per watt'; where 'HBM today is about give or take 21, 22 terabytes per second. We are, like, in hundreds of terabytes per second'. Against SRAM the argument is TCO/area (more racks for the same work). Proof points: the silicon is taped out and 'back in the lab ... coming along very well', with silicon validation and engineering plus commercial samples on track. Generation 1 is 'slated to be commercial and shipping in 2027'; generation 2 lands in 2028 and is benchmarked against HBM4E, where Malladi says the relative gain looks even better because more arithmetic is moving into the logic die under the DRAM stack.

data.signal: CALL-ONLY / QUALCOMM WARNS THAT HBM IS CROWDING OUT HANDSET DRAM. CEO Cristiano Amon: 'As memory suppliers redirect manufacturing capacity to HBM to meet AI data center demand, the resulting industry-wide memory shortage and price increases are likely to define the overall scale of the handset industry through the fiscal year.' In Q&A he called the March-quarter handset weakness '100% related to memory'. Handset demand and sell-through are strong, but 'DRAM availability for consumer electronics, especially handsets, is actually down bias on a year-over-year because of the prioritization of HBM for data centers', so customers are cutting builds to fit the memory they can get. Management added that 'memory vendors have prioritized the build out of HBM' and that memory supply for consumer electronics has been below demand, with similar commentary now coming from gaming consoles and other consumer devices. On duration: 'We can't really predict if this will continue for 2027 or 2028'. The answer depends on planned capacity build-outs and how fast the data-center trend accelerates. The issue 'is not just the price. The issue is just availability'. OEMs are expected to prioritize the premium and high tiers, and automotive is 'a little bit less sensitive to memory price increases'.

The large-load contracting framework has four pillars: long-term contracts (the OpenAI contract is 25 years), minimum bills covering at least 100% of the incremental cost to serve, default/termination provisions, and default payments tied to collateral. Poroch said forms of collateral include parent guarantees, lines of credit and surety bonds depending on counterparty credit quality, with the aim of a collateral portfolio equivalent to about A- or better. He initially cited '$20.8 billion of collateral... in the aggregate on full ramp' and then clarified that this refers to the entire portfolio: 'the whole portfolio of the 17 GW, we got about $21 billion of collateral.' Minimum bills effectively decouple revenue from actual customer ramp rates, which Womack said often differ from what was predicted at project approval.

data.signal: CALL — THE FIBER-CONTENT-PER-GPU FRAMEWORK (the definitive supply-side math for optical in AI factories). Base case: enterprise grows at the rate GPUs grow; THREE drivers add on top. (1) CLUSTER SIZE: clusters ABOVE ~130,000 GPUs exceed a 512-radix switch's two-layer span and need a THIRD OPTICAL LAYER -> ~50% MORE CONTENT PER GPU for very large clusters. (2) BANDWIDTH (doubles ~every 2 years): Hopper -> Blackwell kept 100G SerDes so fibers went 8 -> 16 per GPU (content DOUBLED); the RUBIN era jumps SerDes to 200G with lane count flat -> NEUTRAL; Feynman (~2029-30): fibers double again IF SerDes stays 200G, neutral if 400G arrives (BiDi/WDM could offset) — Springboard conservatively assumes NEUTRAL. (3) SCALE-UP, today 100% COPPER: Vera Rubin Ultra NVL576 is a HYBRID step — copper inside each 72-GPU rack, DIRECT OPTICAL rack-to-rack. Bracketing a full-optical scale-up: 14.4 Tbps scale-up / 200G = 72 lanes x 2 fibers = 144, plus scale-out 1.6 Tbps / 200G = 16 fibers -> 160 FIBERS PER GPU = 10x today's 16-fiber scale-out-only content (reality lands between; % of optical ports is confidential). COMBINED: optical content per GPU +1.3-1.5x BY 2028 and 'much, much higher' toward 2030. Status: Q2 enterprise strength is 'ALL JUST SCALE-OUT — we are not yet seeing scale-up or photonics in our results'; orders accelerating; 'if we could make more, we could sell more.'
data.figure: Content/GPU drivers: 3rd optical layer >130k GPUs (+50%); Blackwell 16 fibers; full-optical scale-up = 160 fibers/GPU (10x); +1.3-1.5x by 2028

data.signal: CALL — PHOTONICS: A $10B MAP BY 2030, AND THE LTA MODEL: Corning's new PHOTONICS Market-Access Platform targets $10 BILLION of revenue by 2030 — passive photonics INSIDE THE BOX (FAU harnesses and everything that moves/manages light between the faceplate and the silicon-photonics optical engine) for CPO/NPO, where Corning historically had ZERO content; likely starts with scale-out, and optical SCALE-UP supercharges it; the plan is built on 'assumptions and discussions AND AGREEMENTS with customers.' Despite industry chatter on scale-up timing, 'NO CHANGES to our fundamental belief... inside the real ecosystem there is much less drama than what it looks like from outside.' Business model: long-term agreements (Amazon multi-billion, NVIDIA, Meta up-to-$6B, Apple) will be 'the LION'S SHARE of our optical business' — every major capacity expansion is underpinned by risk/reward-sharing LTAs; profitability comes from innovation value-share, not bare-fiber pricing (optical NI +77% to a record 21% margin). Springboard math: run rate $20B by end-2026 (Q3 guide may hit it a QUARTER EARLY) -> $30B (2028) -> $40B (2030), 19% CAGR; high-confidence variant $27B/$35B; biggest risk-adjustment between the two = SCALE-UP TIMING. Management calls it a proof point and says it is talking to a number of other players in the market.

The phase III CLARITY-Gastric01 trial of sonesitatug vedotin demonstrated an overall survival benefit in patients with CLDN18.2 expression as low as 25% at any staining intensity, a lower threshold than that required by other CLDN18.2 targeted therapies. Dave Fredrickson said the company expanded the definition of CLDN18.2 positivity with a cutoff of greater than 25%, which represents about half of patients with gastric GEJ cancer, or more than 180,000 patients across the U.S., EU5, China and Japan. Management estimated peak year revenue of $3 billion-$5 billion for the ADC.
data.figure: CLDN18.2 cutoff >25%; ~50% of 2L+ gastric patients; >180,000 patients; peak revenue $3B-$5B

data.signal: Biomarker testing infrastructure was flagged as a commercial gating factor. For Truqap in PTEN-deficient metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer following the CAPItello-281 approval, management said 'a near-term priority is to establish testing in the setting, which today is not common practice.' Truqap revenue was $233 million in the quarter, up 37%. In the AVANZAR trial both the intention-to-treat and the TROP2 biomarker-positive populations sit at the top of the multiple testing procedure, so a positive study can come from either group. For Ultomiris in HSCT-TMA, discussions with health authorities are ongoing on interpreting the data 'including in the context of real-world evidence.'
data.figure: Truqap revenue $233M (+37%)

data.signal: Core R&D expense increased 6% in the first half and represented 23% of total revenue; management expects full-year R&D at the upper end of the low 20s percentage range as it builds out bispecifics, cell therapies and T-cell engagers. Capital expenditure was $1.5 billion in the first half and is expected to increase by around a third in 2026, including a new ADC manufacturing facility in Singapore, and the company opened a new Kendall Square R&D center in Cambridge. Deal-related payments totaled $3.3 billion and new BD transactions totaled just over $2 billion in upfront payments year to date.
data.figure: core R&D +6%, 23% of revenue; H1 capex $1.5B, +~1/3 in 2026; deal payments $3.3B; BD upfronts >$2B YTD

data.signal: Six high-value phase III programs read out positively in the first half, including first pivotal data for three new molecular entities, and the company secured 30 major market approvals. Pascal Soriot said 25 key phase III trial readouts are planned over the next 18 months, with pivotal data readouts for six new molecular entities in 2027 alone. Saruparib in prostate cancer was singled out as a $5 billion-range opportunity reading out next year.
data.figure: 25 phase III readouts in 18 months; 6 NME pivotal readouts in 2027; 30 major market approvals in H1

data.signal: First-half total revenue grew 6%, or 11% excluding Farxiga and Brilinta which are affected by generics, and core EPS grew 11%. Oncology total revenue grew 15% to $14.1 billion with the U.S. up 18% and Europe up 16%; Rare Disease grew 11% to $4.9 billion; BioPharmaceuticals declined 5% to $11.2 billion on loss of exclusivity for Farxiga, Brilinta and roxadustat. Core gross margin was 83% in the first half.
data.figure: total revenue +6% (+11% ex-Farxiga/Brilinta); core EPS +11%; oncology $14.1B (+15%); rare disease $4.9B (+11%); BioPharma $11.2B (-5%); core gross margin 83%

data.signal: Full-year guidance was reiterated: total revenue to increase by a mid-to-high single-digit percentage and core EPS by a low double-digit percentage at constant exchange rates. Management reaffirmed the risk-adjusted $80 billion revenue ambition for 2030, noting 11 approved new molecular entities against a target of 20 by 2030, and said it does not need additional business development to deliver post-2030 growth.
data.figure: revenue mid-to-high single digit; core EPS low double digit CER; $80B by 2030; 11 of 20 NMEs approved

data.signal: Second-quarter regulatory output: Pascal Soriot said the company 'received eight major market approvals across important indications, including two additional NMEs.' These included the first approvals for Enhertu in first-line hormone receptor-positive breast cancer with emergent ESR1 mutations in Europe and Japan and a few other countries, with constructive discussions continuing with the U.S. FDA, and U.S. FDA approval for Baxfendy, 'which has the potential to transform outcomes for patients with uncontrolled or resistant hypertension.' For the first half he identified the two first NME approvals as camizestrant in breast cancer and Baxfendy in hypertension.
data.figure: 8 major market approvals in Q2 including two additional NMEs

data.signal: China: Pascal Soriot said growth 'was impacted by continued effects from volume-based procurement, and we expect the recent NRDL additions and new regulatory approval in 2026 to fuel future growth,' while the U.S., Europe and emerging markets outside of China grew strongly. Asked whether he was still confident on the country, he said he remains 'still very bullish for reasons that have evolved' - Chinese companies are innovating at great speed and tend to partner with global companies to globalize development and commercialization, competition in the Tagrisso market and the ADC market is very intense, and being strongly present in China let the Chinese team play a role in the speedy development of Sone-Ve.
data.figure: no specific figure

data.signal: Core P&L detail below the top line. CFO Aradhana Sarin said product revenue grew 6% in the first half while alliance revenue increased by 29%, 'reflecting higher profit shares from our partnered medicines Enhertu, Datverzo, and Tezspire in markets where our partners record product sales.' Core gross margin of 83% improved in the second quarter compared to the first, but a lower second-half margin is expected 'consistent with prior years, reflecting seasonal demand patterns for lower-margin medicines such as FluMist and Beyfortus,' with full-year core gross margin stable to slightly higher versus 2025. Core SG&A expense also increased by 6% in the first half, covering the U.S. Baxfendy launch and pre-launch investment ahead of tozorakimab. Other operating income was $341 million in the first six months, consisting of royalties and small regional divestitures, with a broadly similar level anticipated in the second half; in Q&A she added there is a portion of it 'that is consistent and will likely continue into 2027.' Guidance for 2027 will be given at the beginning of 2027, after an annual budgeting process that starts later this year.
data.figure: product revenue +6%; alliance revenue +29%; core gross margin 83% in H1; core SG&A +6%; other operating income $341M

data.signal: Cash, working capital and capital structure. Aradhana Sarin reported '$1.2 billion in the first half, a decline versus comparator period' (the transcript drops the line-item label), which 'primarily reflects the Lynparza milestone received in the first quarter of 2025, skewing comparisons, as well as working capital impact associated with U.S. loss of exclusivity for Farxiga'; those working capital effects are expected to persist through the remainder of the year before normalizing. The second-quarter tax rate benefited from a one-time adjustment to deferred tax assets following certain internal legal entity changes. Deal-related payments included the $1.2 billion upfront payment for the CSPC collaboration, which closed during the second quarter, and the company continues to expect milestone payments of approximately $2.5 billion for the full year relating to prior business development transactions, with the most recently announced Dizal transaction included in the year-to-date BD upfronts. Net debt increased by around $3.5 billion in the first half, primarily reflecting the second FY 2025 interim dividend paid in March and those deal payments; the company remains comfortable with its level of gross debt, and core finance costs are expected to be higher in the second half following refinancing at higher than historic interest rates and lower interest income.
data.figure: $1.2B in H1 (decline vs comparator period); CSPC upfront $1.2B; FY milestone payments ~$2.5B; net debt +~$3.5B

data.signal: EGFR-mutated lung franchise. Dave Fredrickson said Tagrisso delivered 6% growth in the second quarter to revenues of $1.9 billion, supported by double-digit growth in the U.S., and that it is the number one prescribed third-generation EGFR TKI globally, approved across all stages of disease; in the highly competitive U.S. market FLAURA2 holds around three-quarters of the growing first-line combination segment. Against the MARIPOSA regimen and intense Chinese competition he said 'we're seeing double-digit volume growth, and in fact, double-digit revenue growth in the U.S.' AstraZeneca also announced the in-licensing of Zegfrovy, a novel oral EGFR inhibitor already approved in the U.S. and China for tumors carrying exon 20 insertion mutations following progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy; based on the WU-KONG28 data presented at ASCO, first-line filings have been submitted in China and the U.S. Susan Galbraith said the asset, licensed from Dizal, is also active in non-classical mutations, 'which is about a similar size patient population.'
data.figure: Tagrisso $1.9B (+6%); FLAURA2 ~three-quarters of the U.S. first-line combination segment

data.signal: Calquence grew 16% in the quarter, 'generating more than $1 billion in revenue for the first time in a single quarter,' and Dave Fredrickson said it maintains its position as the leading BTK inhibitor in frontline CLL across major markets despite intense competition. Within the finite duration class, AMPLIFY continues to gain share in reimbursed markets with encouraging early signs in the U.S., where it is uniquely positioned as the only BTK inhibitor with both finite and treat-to-progression options; management sees AMPLIFY as a significant growth driver through the remainder of 2026, supported by the clear global trend towards adoption of finite duration treatments.
data.figure: Calquence +16%; more than $1 billion in a single quarter for the first time

data.signal: Imfinzi and Imjudo delivered growth of 25% in aggregate in the second quarter, with meaningful contributions from MATTERHORN in gastric cancer and ADRIATIC in lung. Susan Galbraith reported that the phase III VOLGA interim analysis in muscle-invasive bladder cancer, covering 'the 50% of patients who are not candidates for cisplatin,' showed Imfinzi in combination with enfortumab vedotin delivering statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in both event-free survival and overall survival, while the Imjudo-containing arm showed a statistically significant improvement in event-free survival with a favorable trend in overall survival. Positive NILE results also came this quarter, and VOLGA complements NIAGARA and the recently U.S.-approved POTOMAC indication in earlier-stage non-muscle-invasive disease.
data.figure: Imfinzi and Imjudo +25% aggregate in Q2; VOLGA addresses the 50% of patients not candidates for cisplatin

data.signal: Enhertu grew 31% in the quarter to reported revenues of $888 million, with growth across all regions reflecting sustained market leadership in the HER2-positive and HER2-low breast cancer indications in major markets plus increased adoption and additional launches in emerging markets. Dave Fredrickson cited encouraging early signs of adoption and growing awareness in the first-line DESTINY-Breast09 setting in the United States following its approval late last year, and said the recent simultaneous U.S. approvals of DESTINY-Breast05 and DESTINY-Breast11 in the curative setting will become increasingly important through the remainder of the year.
data.figure: Enhertu $888M (+31%)

data.signal: Datroway revenues of $55 million in the second quarter showed growing demand in later-line EGFR-mutated lung cancer with increasing second-line utilization in the U.S., and the launch in triple-negative breast cancer for patients who are not candidates for immunotherapy is underway following the U.S. approval of TROPION-Breast02 earlier in the quarter. Susan Galbraith argued AstraZeneca has 'a best-in-class TROP2-based ADC based on the design, which is based on the stable linker,' pointing to the half-life of the molecule and a lower rate of bone marrow toxicity than ADCs with less stable linkers and more exposure to the free payload. Two phase III trials read out later this year in the post-TKI second-line setting - TROPION-Lung15 (Datroway alone and in combination with Tagrisso) and SAFFRON (Tagrisso combined with Orpathys in MET-driven resistance) - while TROPION-Lung14 aims to bring the Datroway plus Tagrisso combination into the first line.
data.figure: Datroway $55M in Q2

data.signal: CLARITY-Gastric01 trial detail and the wholly-owned ADC franchise. Susan Galbraith said the trial met its overall survival dual primary endpoint with a statistically significant and highly clinically meaningful improvement versus investigator's choice of therapy in patients treated with at least two prior therapies, that there was a trend to PFS benefit which did not meet statistical significance, and that the key secondary endpoint also showed a highly clinically meaningful overall survival benefit in patients treated with at least one prior line. 'Fewer than 20% of patients with advanced gastric cancer survive beyond one year.' Sone-Ve is the first phase III data from the wholly-owned ADC portfolio, the second AstraZeneca ADC to demonstrate an overall survival benefit in gastric cancer after Enhertu, and the third positive phase III readout in this tumor type in just two years following MATTERHORN and DESTINY-Gastric04. The first-line CLARITY-Gastric02 study has a PD-L1 greater than 1% cohort and a less than 1% cohort, combining Sone-Ve with capecitabine with or without Rilvegostomig or nivolumab, and CLDN18.2 is also expressed on some pancreatic and biliary tract cancers being explored in ongoing phase I.
data.figure: fewer than 20% of patients with advanced gastric cancer survive beyond one year

data.signal: Breast and prostate phase III design detail. On camizestrant, Susan Galbraith said SERENA-4 has 'a larger sample size, 1,370 patients enrolled compared to PERSEVERE,' is designed to enrich for endocrine sensitivity, and is anticipated to read out in the second half of this year; she described an overall tolerability profile with low rates of GI side effects and a very low discontinuation rate. CAMBRIA-1 is an extended adjuvant switch trial in intermediate-to-high-risk hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative patients who have completed two-five years of adjuvant endocrine therapy with or without a CDK4/6 inhibitor, which she said selects for an endocrine-sensitive population and 'has a good probability of success.' For saruparib, EvoPAR-Prostate01 is in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer and is powered for both the HRRM and non-HRRM cohorts, taking the learnings from PROpel into an earlier line, with the EvoPAR-Breast opportunity alongside it.
data.figure: SERENA-4: 1,370 patients enrolled, readout in the second half of this year; CAMBRIA-1 enrolls patients who completed two-five years of adjuvant endocrine therapy

data.signal: BioPharmaceuticals second-quarter product performance. Ruud Dobber said respiratory and immunology total revenue grew by 11%, with the established biologics for severe asthma generating 'over $2 billion of in-market sales in the first half.' Fasenra grew 13% to $570 million on continued IL-5 class leadership and grew 75% in emerging markets thanks to its launch in China, where it entered the National Reimbursement Drug List at the start of the year. Tezspire grew by 45% to $390 million. Breztri grew 20% to $346 million, received its first approval for asthma this year in the United States and a positive CHMP recommendation for asthma in Europe last week. Symbicort revenues of $671 million were down 8% on U.S. price pressure from a new generic competitor entering the market. Saphnelo increased 24% to $209 million on share gains in the intravenous segment for SLE patients, with a new subcutaneous formulation now available in the U.S. and some European markets.
data.figure: R&I revenue +11%; severe asthma biologics >$2B in-market H1; Fasenra $570M (+13%, EM +75%); Tezspire $390M (+45%); Breztri $346M (+20%); Symbicort $671M (-8%); Saphnelo $209M (+24%)

data.signal: Farxiga loss of exclusivity and its lifecycle defense. Ruud Dobber said generic competition entered the U.S. at the start of the quarter and that this, along with loss of exclusivity in some other markets and VBP in China, 'saw Farxiga decline by 90% overall, resulting in $1.8 billion of revenue for the quarter.' Three fixed-dose combinations are in development: Zibo-Depa, in phase III and recruiting very fast in proteinuria CKD; Balci-Depa in heart failure patients with a low eGFR where mortality is normally twice that of a normal heart failure patient and where 'more than 12 million patients in the top eight markets are eligible for a treatment like this'; and baxdrostat in combination with dapagliflozin in chronic kidney disease and hypertension. Data for both fixed-dose combinations are expected in the first half of 2027, building on dapagliflozin, of which Dobber said '60 million patients are currently treated.'
data.figure: Farxiga -90% to $1.8B revenue for the quarter; >12 million eligible patients in the top eight markets; 60 million patients currently treated with dapagliflozin; FDC data in H1 2027

data.signal: Baxfendy launch and the primary aldosteronism opportunity. Ruud Dobber said the U.S. approval and launch were secured in May and the company is building early market access through affordability programs, with commercial access expected to broaden over the next few quarters 'in anticipation of Medicare Part D reimbursements from 2028.' Sharon Barr said primary aldosteronism is the leading cause of secondary hypertension and 'could affect as many as 5%-10% of all hypertensives and up to 20% of resistant hypertension,' that relatively few of those patients are screened today because there has been no therapy to give them, and that AstraZeneca has 'the first approved aldosterone synthase inhibitor'; the primary aldosteronism study has accrued very rapidly and the company is accelerating that timeline.
data.figure: primary aldosteronism could affect as many as 5%-10% of all hypertensives and up to 20% of resistant hypertension; Medicare Part D reimbursement from 2028

data.signal: Respiratory pipeline. Sharon Barr said the highly clinically meaningful OBERON and TITANIA phase III results for tozorakimab in COPD will be presented at the European Respiratory Society Congress in September, describing a potential first and best-in-class asset, and Pascal Soriot said that as a result 'we have increased our peak revenue expectation to more than $5 billion' for a product very few people thought would work and to which AstraZeneca itself had assigned a low probability of success. Ruud Dobber attributed the result to a mechanism 'inhibiting the anti-inflammatory pathway, but equally the mucus pathway,' and said the company is 'making an early start on our launch preparations for tezepelumab' (as spoken while describing the OBERON and TITANIA COPD data). Elsewhere in respiratory, the inhaled TSLP Sunakiment, formerly referred to as AZD8630, read out its phase II study with phase III plans under discussion with partner Amgen, and AstraZeneca entered an exclusive license agreement with CTTQ, a subsidiary of Sino Biopharmaceutical, for the development, manufacturing and commercialization of TQC3721, an inhaled small molecule PDE3/4 inhibitor already in phase III trials in China for COPD.
data.figure: tozorakimab peak revenue expectation increased to more than $5 billion

data.signal: The CARDIO-TTRansform miss and how it unwinds against the 2026 readout cohort. Sharon Barr said that in a contemporary ATTR cardiomyopathy population treated with standard of care, 'including 57% on a stabilizer,' adding Wainua did not provide a statistically significant benefit on the composite outcome of CV mortality and recurrent CV events; a pre-specified subgroup of patients on Wainua monotherapy showed fewer primary composite events, a nominally significant result, while no treatment effect was observed in patients on stabilizer therapy at baseline. AstraZeneca and Ionis will analyze the full data set and present at the European Society of Cardiology Congress in August. Aradhana Sarin said the $10 billion figure was 'the peak year estimates with the risk unwind' for the 2026 cohort, that some have unwound in a positive manner like Tozo and some not so positively like Wainua, and that 'I still think we'll unwind close to $10 billion' - not a 2030 number, since peak for some of these products may hit beyond 2030. Pascal Soriot added that AstraZeneca owns tozorakimab 100% whereas Wainua was to be shared with partner Ionis, so 'we gained more with Tozo than we lost with Wainua.'
data.figure: 57% on a stabilizer in CARDIO-TTRansform; 2026 cohort still expected to unwind close to $10 billion in peak year sales

data.signal: Cardiometabolic pipeline. Sharon Barr said the phase II-B VISTA trial of the oral GLP-1 elecoglipron showed 'a clinically meaningful and statistically significant weight loss of up to 11.8% at week 36, importantly, without evidence of a plateau,' while SOLSTICE showed 'an up to 1.9% reduction in HbA1c at week 26,' with a favorable safety profile and low discontinuation rates. First subject in was achieved for both EMBOLD (monotherapy in obesity or overweight) and ILLUMINATE (five phase III trials in Type 2 diabetes, as monotherapy and in combination with dapagliflozin), and ELEVATE is planned in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and chronic kidney disease; Pascal Soriot said 'we have now initiated five phase III trials for elecoglipron.' Beyond GLP-1, the phase II APRICUS trial of the selective amylin receptor agonist AZD6234 read out this quarter with a phase III monotherapy trial now initiating and data to be shared at EASD; the oral PCSK9 lariprostat has a phase III readout in the first half of 2027 with a first fixed-dose combination of lariprostat with rosuvastatin advancing into phase III, and Soriot said a further fixed-dose combination with elecoglipron is being developed. Ruud Dobber said the competitor's official first U.S. list price 'will not change dramatically our own outlook.'
data.figure: VISTA weight loss up to 11.8% at week 36; SOLSTICE up to 1.9% HbA1c reduction at week 26; five phase III trials initiated for elecoglipron; oral PCSK9 phase III readout in H1 2027

data.signal: Rare Disease medicine-level performance. Marc Dunoyer said second-quarter Ultomiris grew 12% on patient demand across indications including the competitive MG and PNH markets, while Soliris revenues continued to decline due to successful conversion to Ultomiris as well as biosimilar pressure. Strensiq grew 36% year-on-year and 'remains one of AstraZeneca's fastest-growing blockbuster medicines,' supported by ongoing investment in commercial capabilities, infrastructure and disease awareness that also lays the foundation for the potential launch of efzimfotase alfa. Vosoritide continued to deliver strong global momentum, supported by expansion in adult patients with NF1-PN and uptake of the granule formulation in recently launched markets, and remained the market leader for pediatric patients with NF1-PN.
data.figure: Ultomiris +12%; Strensiq +36%

data.signal: Complement franchise pipeline. Marc Dunoyer said phase III I CAN data for Ultomiris in IgA nephropathy showed 'a 43% reduction in proteinuria, with significant proteinuria reduction seen as early as 10 weeks,' consistent across patient groups including those at higher risk of progression, and the company has now filed in both the U.S. and Japan. In HSCT-TMA, Ultomiris 'did not achieve statistical significance for the primary endpoint of event-free survival through 26 weeks compared to placebo in adults and adolescents aged 12 years older,' though it showed a trend towards treatment benefit; in pediatric patients AstraZeneca is advancing regulatory filings based on the open-label phase III trial reported in 2025 and data from an external control study. Asked about longer-acting C5 competitors, Dunoyer said the franchise continues to grow and the response is to pioneer new indications - IgAN, HSCT-TMA, delayed graft function and other renal rare diseases - and to develop other nodes of complement biology beyond C5.
data.figure: I CAN: 43% reduction in proteinuria, significant reduction as early as 10 weeks; HSCT-TMA primary endpoint of event-free survival through 26 weeks not met

data.signal: efzimfotase alfa in hypophosphatasia. Marc Dunoyer said the phase III pediatric MULBERRY and CHESTNUT data were presented at the International Conference on Children's Bone Health in June, and that in a pooled analysis of the phase III MULBERRY and HICKORY trials including pediatric, adolescent and adult patients, treatment 'resulted in a median of 361 days per year free from injection site reactions,' with injection site reaction rates 'five times lower than with Strensiq'; HICKORY data will be presented at the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research in October. In Q&A he said the filings 'will be above two years of age for a broad population,' done in discussion with regulatory authorities, covering adults with pediatric onset (already obtained in several countries with Strensiq) and adults with adult onset (where Strensiq is not approved today), and that 'even if we get less than the totality of the label that we have filed for, we expect to be within the range of $3 billion-$5 billion.' He contrasted dosing every two weeks against daily or every-other-day Strensiq and said patients on efzimfotase alfa have 'five days of injection site reaction on average in a given year,' which should improve country coverage, label breadth and patient retention.
data.figure: median of 361 days per year free from injection site reactions; ISR rates five times lower than Strensiq; five days of ISR on average per year; filings above two years of age; peak sales within $3 billion-$5 billion

data.signal: Other Rare Disease programs. Marc Dunoyer said phase III CALYPSO data presented in May at ECE showed eneboparatide maintaining serum calcium within the target range, normalizing urinary calcium and restoring normal bone turnover in patients with hypoparathyroidism. For anselamimab in kappa light chain amyloidosis, results from the CARES program 'demonstrated a 62% reduction in all-cause mortality and a 71% reduction in cardiovascular hospitalization,' with an overall survival benefit observed even in patients with advanced Mayo stage disease. On the TTR depleter cliramitug, he said the trial is run 'as an add-on to either stabilizer, tafamidis or acoramidis, and Silences' and not as a monotherapy, that depletion of amyloid burden in the tissues was confirmed during phase I-B studies over one year, and that anselamimab provides a read-across for the depleter mechanism in amyloidosis; Pascal Soriot added that cliramitug can be used as monotherapy, on top of vutrisiran, or on top of stabilizers.
data.figure: anselamimab CARES: 62% reduction in all-cause mortality and 71% reduction in cardiovascular hospitalization

data.signal: Post-2030 growth platforms and the probability-of-success assumption behind the plan. Pascal Soriot said three recent launches - Datverzo, Etcamah and Baxfendy - each carry 'peak year revenue potential of more than $5 billion.' In next-generation IO, 'we now have 16 phase III trials across eight tumor types, including five in combination with our ADCs,' supporting an ambition to replace the current generation of checkpoint inhibitors. AZD0120 and surovatamig each have multiple phase III trials underway across hematology and both have now extended into autoimmune diseases, alongside investment in off-the-shelf and in vivo cell therapies. In ADCs and radioconjugates, phase III data for the second wholly-owned ADC Puxi-Sam are anticipated next year and first phase III trials for tovusam and zagaru were dosed this quarter. On the assumptions, Soriot said 'the average probability of success across phase III for the industry is 60%-65%,' that the aggregate probability of success AstraZeneca uses across its pipeline 'is around 60%,' and that '75%+ has been our record.'
data.figure: Datverzo, Etcamah and Baxfendy each with peak year revenue potential of more than $5 billion; 16 phase III IO trials across eight tumor types including five with ADCs; industry phase III PTS 60%-65% vs around 60% assumed and a 75%+ record

data.signal: Pricing environment and legal. Dave Fredrickson said AstraZeneca does not give brand-specific pricing commentary on most favored nation pricing, but that 'our pricing approach across all of launches now has really evolved in response to MFN,' and with 'the U.S. now referencing a basket of countries and setting its price, we are seeing productive engagement with payers in the wealthy nations within that context.' For Etcamah specifically, early negotiations are reflecting a new reality 'that funding for innovation needs to rise in line with a country's GDP per capita,' those discussions are expected to take more time than in the past, and the U.S. objective of prices in wealthy nations coming up and U.S. prices coming down a bit is 'the direction of travel.' Separately, Ruud Dobber confirmed that as noted in the legal disclosures the company 'started an arbitration process regarding Beyfortus in the United States' and does not comment on arbitration or legal procedures.

On neoclouds: today they run compute against storage that physically sits in the public cloud, so Seagate sells the same drives to the same public-cloud customers; if neoclouds start serving their own customers they 'cannot access the public cloud storage anymore' and will need their own storage, shifting some of that volume directly to neoclouds - positive for customer diversification, roughly neutral on volume.

data.signal: AI DEMAND DRIVERS AND THE HDD STORAGE TIER (CEO Dave Mosley): video keeps driving hard-drive demand. Platforms like YouTube see 20 million video uploads daily, up from just 2 million 3 years ago, and that does not yet include the full surge expected from AI-driven video applications. Agentic AI 'relies on persistent access to large volumes of historic data'. Hard drives anchor the mass-capacity tier, storing the checkpoint data sets used for training and supporting the vector databases that give inference its context. On the warm tier, random small-block workloads are 'probably memory', while big data is 'a little bit of memory on the front end and a lot of hard drive on the back end'. The architectural tier that stores large data such as checkpoints, physical AI and video 'will probably remain constant for the next decade'. Hard drives are not idle background storage: 'They're working 24/7', optimized largely for streaming performance.
data.figure: no specific figure

data.signal: 80% OF THE WORLD'S DATA NOW SITS ON A HARD DRIVE IN THE DATA CENTER - THE MARKET-STRUCTURE NUMBER SEAGATE'S CALLS DO NOT GIVE. Chairman Dave Mosley on how the business moved from the PC era to mass capacity: 'Now all the data, the mass capacity data we call it, is up in data centers. The boxes that have really morphed, the whole supply chain has had to morph over the last 10 years to the point where 80% of the world's data is on a hard drive in the data center right now, and it's continuing to grow at leaps and bounds.' He attributed the acceleration to AI application breadth rather than any single workload: 'the different applications have just exploded... there's so many different fronts where you've got applications pulling data, creating data, sending it back down'. Seagate's earnings calls quantify its own exabytes and the data-center share of its revenue; this is the installed-base share of world data.
data.figure: 80% of the world's data is on a hard drive in the data center right now

data.signal: RETENTION ECONOMICS QUANTIFIED FROM SEAGATE'S OWN CIO RESEARCH: 55% SAY DELETING DATA COST THEM MONEY. Chairman Dave Mosley on a study Seagate ran with CIO-level respondents: 'I'll say 55% of the people answering the survey said, I've lost a lot of money because I deleted something that I shouldn't have deleted.' He was explicit that this is not a compliance cost: 'That's not a penalty, that's not because of compliance issues. That's because of opportunity lost, because they deleted something.' Seagate applies the same logic internally - 'Running factories ourselves, we see this every day. If we could only store information about what's going on in the factories for a little bit longer, we believe you can get utility out of that' - and expects the same on customer-acquisition and customer-service data elsewhere. This is the demand-side mechanism (delete-less behaviour) behind the retention narrative the calls assert but never size.
data.figure: 55% of the people answering the survey said they lost money by deleting something they should not have deleted

data.signal: COLD/OFFLINE STORAGE LOSES ITS ROLE AND NEARLINE BECOMES THE PREFERENTIAL TIER. Asked whether cold storage becomes a non-discussion because data now has to be hot or at least readily accessible, Chairman Dave Mosley drew the line at accessibility rather than temperature: 'We call our products nearline products. These monikers, I don't think we've all come up with the right language yet. But, to me, cold storage means it's so far offline that it's virtually unusable unless a human brings it back... That probably is not going to be very efficient in the future. I think if we can continue to really drive our technology hard and grow exabytes in our industry, then that nearline will become the preferential storage mechanism.' The condition he attaches is Seagate's own areal-density execution - the tier shift only happens if the industry keeps growing exabytes at cost.
data.figure: no specific figure

data.signal: OBJECT STORES PLUS METADATA-IN-MEMORY ARE THE ARCHITECTURE CHANGE THAT PUTS UNSTRUCTURED DATA BACK ON HDD TIERS. Chairman Dave Mosley on the stack above the drive: 'down inside the storage layer, we've always been kind of subservient to the file systems and things above us. Now we're starting to see more what I'll call object stores. Where what's really happening at layers above us, in memory layers, say, is that you are having very fast transactions on metadata, then when you need that specific data underneath, you pull it up. That architecture was never really honed before, but it is now. What that means is all of this, the data can be stored cheaper, relatively cheaper, and you can store a lot more of it on the hard drive tiers.' In some cases 'the unstructured data is not even used, it is just the metadata around the unstructured data. You only know which data you need when the algorithm tells you you need it, you pull it up.' He also described the software stack becoming less lossy with fewer handoffs - 'People don't want to pay for that. They want to pay for actually data in the application' - producing 'a stronger tie between the ultimate application, call it agentic application if you want, down through the software stack and into the hardware'.
data.figure: no specific figure

data.signal: CUSTOMERS NOW PUSH ON ACCESS SPEED PER DRIVE, NOT ONLY CAPACITY - AND ON DATA SOVEREIGNTY. Asked what could shift the conversation three years out, Chairman Dave Mosley put two vectors on the roadmap: 'We're going to keep driving density, and we think we can, which is great, makes the data centers more efficient. We can also drive the technology that actually makes the data more accessible on each individual hard drive or at the system level. We're going to get pushed very hard on that because it's not only more data, it's also data faster, which are the vectors that our customers are really driving.' Beyond the drive itself he flagged data protection and locality - 'making sure that you have the right data in the right location, that it's actually my data and not shared with everybody in the world... Sometimes it's called sovereign data' - as a topic he expects to get much more discussion. Closing: 'These trends are happening in our favor, and we know there is a lot riding on our shoulders. We have to keep our technology going forward so that we can keep gaining efficiency.'
data.figure: no specific figure

data.signal: THE CORE THESIS, sharpened: 'While COMPUTE CYCLES CAN BE REUSED, DATA COMPOUNDS.' Training creates the initial data foundation, inference generates data continuously, agentic systems multiply the volume and frequency, and physical AI accelerates the cycle further - so storage demand shifts from a one-time infrastructure build to the ongoing compounding of retained data. The largest AI platforms now process TENS OF BILLIONS OF TOKENS PER MINUTE and BILLIONS OF PROMPTS PER DAY with token volumes growing severalfold YoY. Roughly 80% OF DATA STORED IN A HYPERSCALE DATA CENTER SITS ON HARD DISK DRIVES, and management expects that to hold. For PHYSICAL AI (autonomous vehicles, robotics, humanoids, industrial automation) real-world data is INSUFFICIENT to train the models, so operators generate and must store SYNTHETIC DATA SETS for reinforcement learning - a new demand vector. On inference specifically: storing generated context is MORE ECONOMICAL THAN RE-RUNNING IT through compute and memory. Core cloud services (notably stored video/collaboration recordings) remain an underappreciated parallel driver, and cheaper open-source Asian models are viewed as demand-positive since more model access means more data
data.figure: ~80% of hyperscale data on HDD; tens of billions of tokens/min; synthetic data for physical AI

data.signal: Management listed four new and developing uses of battery storage by large energy users such as data centers and C&I facilities. (1) Speed to power: storage speeds grid interconnection by matching power demand to grid capability and avoids the delays and expense of grid upgrades. (2) Quality of power: injecting reactive power to resolve voltage disturbances, managing demand (including disconnecting from the grid when needed) and smooth ramp-rate control. (3) Backup power: replacing higher-cost, carbon-intensive thermal gensets. (4) Support of on-site, bring-your-own generation behind the meter. Quality of power needs a response time below ten milliseconds; Fluence has a road map to deliver it, and this is where it competes with other technologies. Current data-center demand comes more from speed-to-power and bring-your-own-generation applications than from quality of power. Management cited product density, safety, reliability and cybersecurity as advantages, and noted that Fluence does not compete with its data-center customers.
data.figure: response time below ten milliseconds (quality-of-power requirement)

data.signal: U.S. DOMESTIC SUPPLY CHAIN: the domestic-content supply chain now performs at the level the delivery schedule needs. Cell and module production is running ahead of plan, the enclosure manufacturing facility in Arizona is now on track, and the domestic supplier base is being expanded and diversified. On battery cells, Fluence is working with ASC (named AESC in the analyst's question) to resolve the prohibited foreign entity (PFE) status of ASC's Tennessee facility. Fluence made ASC an ownership proposal, but ASC gave assurances that it will meet the law's conditions another way, without Fluence joining the ownership structure; Fluence's priority is competitively priced, PFE-compliant cells. The 2026 delivery plan uses a roughly half-and-half mix of domestic and imported cells. Several U.S. facilities are converting EV battery lines to storage production; management compares this to China two or three years ago and sees it diversifying the supplier base toward multiple domestic cell partners. Management sees no real change in the competitive environment, only a significant diversification of battery-cell suppliers. It sees no need for vertical integration: contract manufacturers build Fluence's designs, and its system can integrate three or four different battery manufacturers.
data.figure: domestic vs imported cell mix roughly half and half (2026 delivery plan)

The FDA also cleared the IND for VX-017, the type O or universal donor islet cell product, which management said would double the Type 1 Diabetes market opportunity from about 60,000 to about 120,000 patients.

Interim analysis results from the AMPLITUDE phase III study in AMKD remain on track for early 2027, AMPLIFY results are expected this fall and initial VX-828 patient data in the second half of this year.

data.signal: CFO Charlie Wagner broke cystic fibrosis revenue out by geography. Q2 2026 U.S. CF revenue grew 9% year-over-year, led by strong volume growth from ALYFTREK uptake, continued performance from TRIKAFTA and higher realized net price, while CF revenue outside the U.S. grew 12% year-over-year, driven by strong ALYFTREK launches, timing of orders in certain geographies and the benefit from FX. Global CF revenue growth for the first half of 2026 was 8%, including the benefit of prior year U.S. price increases and foreign exchange, both of which management expects to contribute less to growth in the second half of the year. Q2 2025 results also included $21 million of collaboration revenue.

data.signal: Chief Commercial Officer Duncan McKechnie said ALYFTREK crossed another significant milestone, exceeding $1 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026. In the U.S. patients are initiating ALYFTREK new to therapy, returning to therapy and switching from TRIKAFTA, with the majority of ALYFTREK revenue continuing to come from TRIKAFTA switch patients, and uptake accelerated from the recent approvals in rare mutations as well as patients rolling off open label extension studies. Outside the U.S., with no requirement for augmented liver monitoring in the E.U., more than one in three eligible CF patients in Germany and the U.K. are now benefiting from ALYFTREK.
data.figure: ALYFTREK revenue exceeded $1 billion in 1H 2026; majority of revenue from TRIKAFTA switch patients; more than one in three eligible CF patients on ALYFTREK in Germany and the U.K.

data.signal: CEO Reshma Kewalramani said data presented at ECFS reinforced that ALYFTREK best restores CFTR function amongst the available CFTR modulators: among children with CF under 12 years of age the majority across all eligible genotypes achieve a sweat chloride less than 30 millimoles, nearly 2/3 of younger patients achieved sweat chloride levels less than 30 millimole per liter, and for patients ages 12+ more than 75% achieved sweat chloride levels within the carrier range of CFTR function. She said the unmet need is far lower today and the bar for any medicine to beat ALYFTREK is very, very high, so Vertex will only advance next gen 3.0 assets into phase II and beyond that show promise to beat ALYFTREK with once daily dosing and excellent drug-like properties including drug-drug interactions.
data.figure: nearly 2/3 of younger patients to sweat chloride less than 30 millimole per liter; more than 75% of patients ages 12+ within the carrier range

data.signal: Vertex has initiated global regulatory submissions for ALYFTREK in children ages two to five, and global regulatory submissions for TRIKAFTA in patients ages one to two are also in progress. Duncan McKechnie said the CF growth drivers for the remainder of 2026 are continued ALYFTREK uptake, the label expansion into rare mutations, younger patients and additional geographies.
data.figure: ALYFTREK submissions in children ages two to five; TRIKAFTA submissions in patients ages one to two

data.signal: Duncan McKechnie said the $76 million of CASGEVY revenue reflected approximately 75% sequential growth versus quarter one 2026 and over 150% year-over-year growth, in line with expectations based on visibility into patient scheduling patterns. There were more CASGEVY infusions in the first half of 2026 than in all of 2025, and the second quarter was the third sequential quarter with more than 100 patient initiations, which enhances visibility to continued growth for the rest of this year and early 2027 as patients continue to move through cell collection, editing and infusion. Quarter-to-quarter variability in CASGEVY revenue will continue and reflects the timing of patient infusions.

data.signal: New data on CASGEVY at EHA, with simultaneous publication in the New England Journal of Medicine, demonstrated its transformative potential in pediatric patients as well as durable benefits. Last month CASGEVY became the first and only gene therapy FDA approved to treat children as young as two years old in both sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia, receiving supplemental approval in the U.S. in a record 53 days post-filing, and the first pediatric patient has already initiated therapy and conducted cell collection. Outside the U.S. CASGEVY regulatory submissions in the five to 11 age group are now complete in Saudi Arabia and the United Kingdom.

data.signal: Duncan McKechnie said JOURNAVX revenue of $50 million reflected sequential revenue growth of approximately 70% and sequential prescription growth of approximately 45% versus quarter one 2026, with revenue positively impacted by channel build after a drawdown in quarter one. Vertex continues to expect some quarterly volatility in inventory build and drawdown as full line wholesalers and retail channel buying patterns normalize to reflect formulary adoption, physician awareness and seasonality in elective surgeries. Rapid prescription growth has also driven greater use of the PSP program than forecast; as physicians and their office staff are educated about quantity limits and prior authorizations Vertex expects the PSP to be triggered less frequently and therefore more revenue to be recognized, and gross to net is now expected to normalize in line with other branded oral medicines in the first half of 2027.

data.signal: Quarter two 2026 JOURNAVX prescriptions totaled approximately 535,000 and just over 900,000 for the first half of 2026, split roughly 50/50 between the hospital and retail channels. In both channels monthly prescriptions were approximately 50,000 in January and doubled to approximately 100,000 in each channel in June. Asked about prescribing behavior, Duncan McKechnie said hospital prescription duration is around about five days, retail is around about 12, 14 days, and it nets out at around about 10 or 11 days for each JOURNAVX prescription, a dynamic that has not changed since launch because it is driven by the dynamics of the institution the patient is in.
data.figure: approximately 535,000 prescriptions in Q2 and just over 900,000 in 1H 2026; roughly 50/50 hospital and retail; approximately 50,000 per channel per month in January doubling to approximately 100,000 in June; around 10 or 11 days per prescription

data.figure: approximately 18,000 new HCP prescribers added in Q2; 1,400 hospital and 130 IDN pathways

data.signal: Reshma Kewalramani said POVI is putting up very strong proteinuria numbers, numerically the best out there: a 52% change from baseline in terms of proteinuria reduction, 70+% reductions in hematuria and 70+% reductions in Gd-IgA1, delivered once monthly in a small volume of 0.46 mils via an auto-injector at home. Duncan McKechnie said approximately 70% of U.S. patients with IgAN have commercial coverage, payer awareness of IgAN and the new BAFF/APRIL inhibitors is high, and Vertex anticipates it will have the largest field force among the novel APRIL or APRIL-BAFF therapies for IgAN. data.signal: In primary membranous nephropathy the OLYMPUS phase II/III pivotal trial has completed its phase II portion, the phase III portion initiated last quarter, and the IDMC has completed its review and selected the phase III dose of 80 mg subcutaneously every four weeks; Reshma Kewalramani said the decision was based on the PLA2R biomarker and was not surprising given the RUBY-3 results, where the 80 mg had a very nice reduction in PLA2R. Vertex holds fast track, orphan drug and EMA Prime designations for POVI in membranous. Outside renal, the 30-patient phase II proof of concept study of POVI in myasthenia gravis, evaluating 80 mg and 240 mg doses versus placebo for 12 weeks, is on track to complete enrollment by the end of this year.

data.signal: On AMPLITUDE, the pivotal phase II/III study of inaxaplin in AMKD, Vertex completed enrollment of the interim analysis cohort in September of last year and is on track to complete full enrollment by the end of this year, with the interim analysis conducted following 48 weeks of treatment. Reshma Kewalramani said Vertex has an agreement with the agency for a potential accelerated approval based on the primary endpoint at the time of the interim analysis, which is one-year GFR, in patients with two APOL1 alleles, moderate to heavy proteinuria and depressed GFR, and that a positive result would position Vertex to file for potential accelerated approval in the U.S. thereafter.

The AGLOW phase II proof of concept study of VX-407 in ADPKD has completed enrollment and runs with up to 52 weeks of treatment.
data.figure: AMPLIFIED low proteinuria arm 0.2-0.7 g versus 0.7 g and above, results this fall; AGLOW with up to 52 weeks of treatment

data.signal: Reshma Kewalramani said Vertex had very constructive meetings with the FDA following its voluntary pause to conduct a manufacturing analysis of exemlcel and has resumed dosing patients in the exemlcel phase I/II/III study. A silver lining of the pause is that the type O program time differential versus exemlcel has shortened, so Vertex is considering options to further streamline its regulatory strategy and commercialization approach and may bring type O out first or very close behind, with updated T1D plans including timelines expected in the back half of this year. Vertex also continues to progress serial innovation work on improved immunosuppression and hypoimmune programs.

Exelon supports PJM's reliability backstop option, backs extending the PJM capacity auction collar, and joined Governor Shapiro's FERC filing. On data-center colocation, Exelon's Colette Honorable (named by the CEO on the call) said "Colocation can be a great solution" and that Exelon took its colocation stance to protect affordability. The CFO said new generation must be built at the right price.

data.signal: 2025 revenue drivers: unit-driven revenue grew approximately 2% in 2025, in line with wafer starts, led by CMP consumables, liquid filtration and selective etch. CapEx-driven revenue declined 7%, matching the drop in industry fab construction CapEx, which the CEO described as 'down high single digits, call it seven ish percent'. The drop was most visible in the FOUP and Fluid Handling product lines in the APS division. About 75% of revenue is unit-driven and tracks MSI (wafer starts); the other 25% is tied to industry CapEx. Roughly two-thirds of that CapEx-related revenue follows fab construction spending and one-third follows WFE. Early in 2026, management said order patterns for these CapEx-linked product lines were already starting to recover.

data.signal: End-market mix: more than 60% of Entegris' revenue comes from advanced logic (seven nanometers and below) and advanced memory (the two newest memory generations).
