data.signal: 2026 logic and industry outlook: management expects Entegris to benefit from node transitions in both logic and memory. Rising demand for two-nanometer devices should meaningfully lift wafer output through 2026, and that node carries both higher content per wafer and strong share for Entegris. Advanced logic fab utilization is already near 100%, and customers are investing aggressively in more capacity. At the most advanced logic node, Entegris has secured strong POR (position of record) positions in CMP consumables, advanced deposition and implant materials, liquid purification and filtration, and wafer handling. The team is now focused on winning incremental share and PORs at subsequent advanced nodes. Separately, the CEO said it takes time to grow two-nanometer and to transition to new nodes such as 1.4 nanometer. Management expects 'middish single-digit' industry MSI (wafer starts) growth in 2026 and strong WFE growth. Fab construction CapEx should grow modestly after last year's high single-digit decline, weighted to the second half, with a bigger acceleration in 2027 as work starts on new fabs. Management flagged ongoing memory shortages as a possible second-half 2026 risk for mainstream end markets; guidance assumes no impact.
data.figure: middish single-digit industry MSI growth expected in 2026; advanced logic utilization near 100%

data.signal: NAND: the move from roughly 250 layers to approximately 300 layers is under way. Management expects more than 20% NAND bit growth in 2026, driven mainly by higher-layer, higher-capacity NAND rather than a big increase in wafer starts. Entegris expects a double-digit increase in its NAND content per wafer as customers move to higher layer counts and adopt new materials such as moly and selective etch. It has won strong POR positions in NAND deposition materials, CMP and selective etch. NAND utilization is around 85%, and layer-count increases are absorbing most of the remaining 15% of capacity, with fewer new wafer starts. If demand stays strong, flash makers will likely need to add significant fab capacity, setting up higher NAND MSI growth in 2027. The CEO said Entegris gains from both layer growth and wafer growth, with slightly more from a full wafer start.
data.figure: more than 20% NAND bit growth expected in 2026; double-digit increase in NAND content per wafer; NAND utilization around 85%

data.signal: DRAM, HBM and advanced packaging: DRAM capacity was nearly fully utilized at the end of 2025, and management expects it to stay that way through 2026. More DRAM is shifting from standalone DDR5 into HBM, which adds some content per wafer, though less than a new wafer start would. Management expects tight supply in HBM, DDR5 and advanced packaging to require additional fab capacity heading into 2027. Entegris is gaining traction in DRAM and HBM, particularly with CMP consumables and advanced packaging solutions. The CEO said advanced packaging revenue grew nicely in 2025, to 'roughly a $100 million plus minus', and should keep growing in 2026. Several product lines for advanced packaging are sampling now and more will sample later in the year, so the larger benefit is expected in 2027 and beyond.
data.figure: advanced packaging revenue roughly $100 million (2025), expected to keep growing in 2026

data.signal: Capacity and capex: the multiyear manufacturing capex cycle that began in 2022 is complete. Capex was $299 million in 2025 (approximately 9% of sales) and is expected to fall to $250 million in 2026, returning longer term to approximately 7% to 8% of sales. Management said the new capacity plus the existing base can deliver significantly more than $1 billion in incremental revenue with limited further investment. The Taiwan facility is still ramping, and the Colorado facility should substantially complete key customer product qualifications in 2026. Entegris exited its Chester, Pennsylvania facility in Q4 and expects to rationalize at least one additional facility in 2026. Free cash flow was $404 million in 2025, a 12.7% margin (up nearly 300 basis points year over year). Net leverage ended 2025 at 3.8 times, against a target of below 3.5 times by the end of 2026, and Entegris paid down $300 million of its term loan during 2025.
data.figure: 2025 capex $299 million; 2026 capex expected $250 million; capacity supports significantly more than $1 billion incremental revenue; 2025 free cash flow $404 million (12.7% margin)
